title: Mahler, Symphony No. 5, Adagietto, in two recordings
question: Mengelberg in 1926 and the Peabody Symphony Orchestra play the Adagietto’s violin melody over the harp.
intro: Mahler scored the movement for strings and harp, with a violin melody that repeatedly crosses the bar-line. Mengelberg’s Concertgebouw players slide together between notes and push forward through the short pickups, then slow down when the theme returns. The second performance is by the Peabody Symphony Orchestra, taken from its complete recording of the Fifth.

recordings.label: Peabody Symphony Orchestra
recordings.note: The strings and harp of the Peabody orchestra, from its complete recording of Mahler’s Fifth Symphony.

recordings.label: Willem Mengelberg, Concertgebouw Orchestra, 1926
recordings.note: The strings slide between notes together; Mengelberg urges the opening pickups forward and slows the returning theme.

passages.label: Violin melody over harp
passages.note: The violins play the melody over plucked harp notes. The phrase places its weight on notes that resolve only after a delay.

passages.label: First climax
passages.note: The violins rise higher, with harp arpeggios beneath them. The phrase grows louder, then falls.

passages.label: Return of the opening melody
passages.note: The harp returns beneath the opening tune. Mengelberg takes the start of this return more slowly.

passages.label: High violins, ascending cellos
passages.note: High violins sustain the line while the cellos climb below. Mahler asked for broad bow strokes as the phrase approaches its last swell.
